## 固定收益開盤主論述

原油再度上漲，重燃近期通膨風險，也推高市場對聯準會升息機率的估計，美國公債在7月21日延續跌勢。2年期殖利率上升5.5個基點至4.264%，5年期上升4.8個基點至4.37%，10年期上升3.6個基點至4.629%，30年期上升2個基點至5.133%。曲線前端與中段調整幅度較大，2年期與10年期利差收窄1.9個基點至36.5個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄3.5個基點至86.9個基點。

油價是最明確的催化因素。美國與伊朗連續第10天互相發動攻擊，針對沙烏地阿拉伯航運的威脅也開始改變油輪行為，WTI上漲1.92%至$84.83，布蘭特原油上漲2.87%至$91.78。伊朗支持的胡塞武裝警告，停靠沙烏地港口的船隻可能成為攻擊目標。駛近葉門水域的油輪暫停前進，載運沙烏地原油的船隻則向北轉往蘇伊士運河。沙烏地阿拉伯為繞過受干擾的荷莫茲海峽而改道出口後，這條航線的重要性已經上升，如今也受到威脅。

市場反應並不限於通膨補償。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1.4個基點至2.279%，10年期實質殖利率也上升2.2個基點至2.35%，顯示投資人不只要求補償較不利的通膨前景，也要求承擔存續期風險取得更高實質報酬。利率期貨顯示，7月28日至29日聯準會會議升息的機率約為25%，近幾日略有提高，但仍低於月初約五成的水準。上週溫和通膨數據公布後的債券漲幅已全數回吐。

最新勞動市場資料未釋出廣泛降溫訊號。第2季美國全職工作者每週薪資中位數較一年前增加4.6%，高於消費者物價3.9%的漲幅。6月各州勞動市場大致穩定：8州失業率下降、2州上升，40州及哥倫比亞特區維持不變；僅3州非農就業人數顯著增加，1州減少。這組數據維持了家庭所得支撐，但既未顯示全國就業加速，也未出現足以明確抵銷能源衝擊的惡化。

風險資產表現穩健，使美國公債未能獲得明顯避險買盤。投資人重返先前重挫的晶片股，帶動標普500指數上漲0.89%、那斯達克100指數上漲1.93%，費城半導體指數更勁揚5.21%。不過，半導體指數一個月來仍下跌13.85%，這波反彈只是收復部分失地，尚未扭轉市場近期對AI估值的重新評估。金價上漲1.87%至$4,085.20，美元指數上漲0.19%。股票、原油、黃金與美元同步走高，顯示利率市場聚焦的是通膨與政策，而非各類資產一致撤離風險。

美國以外的主權債殖利率曲線也各有壓力來源。投資人等待新任英國首相安迪·伯納姆與財政大臣約翰·希利說明，如何在有限財政空間下兼顧生活成本援助與國防承諾，英國公債殖利率因而維持在近兩個月高點附近。日本最終經濟計畫確認日本央行的自主性，卻未解決擬議食品減稅的成本與融資問題。歐元區銀行則表示，企業與家庭信貸標準全面收緊。整體而言，能源成本上升之際，各國財政空間受到質疑，先前貨幣緊縮的傳導效應也仍在發揮作用。

信用市場持續分化，改善中的主權發行人、能接觸新資金來源的借款人，以及債券文件或流動性已成為價值核心的企業，表現各不相同。穆迪調升阿根廷評等；印尼啟動首筆熊貓債簿記；Danantara則研議再次發行美元債。壓力較大的一端，Aston Martin債權人升高對潛在擔保品移轉的反對行動；Victoria仍未取得完成協議重整所需的支持；America’s Car-Mart在一筆私人貸款違約後考慮出售資產。高基準殖利率尚未封閉融資市場，卻正使仰賴反覆再融資、寬鬆契約條款或樂觀營運假設的借款人暴露弱點。

## 油價重燃聯準會近期升息風險

美國公債呈現空頭趨平，而非前一交易日的溫和趨陡。2年期殖利率上升5.5個基點，升幅比30年期多3.5個基點，顯示邊際定價調整集中在政策利率展望所牽動的期限。10年期殖利率盤中觸及4.64%，為5月底以來最高；10年期與30年期殖利率收盤也都處於約兩個月高點。

油價上漲使通膨風險的時點更為迫近。戰事再起，加上紅海航運受威脅，布蘭特原油收於$91以上，一週累計上漲8.32%，一個月上漲14.94%；WTI一週上漲6.92%，一個月上漲10.74%。這些累計漲幅對聯準會具有重要意義，因為6月的良性通膨數據反映的是較早期能源環境，市場如今評估的是7月油價持續反彈可能產生的轉嫁效應。

安全問題的地理範圍也進一步擴大。荷莫茲海峽航運原已受到攻擊與伊朗戰事壓力；沙烏地阿拉伯則利用橫跨沙漠的輸油管線及紅海碼頭維持出口，使該路線成為全球供應的重要緩衝。胡塞武裝的警告威脅往返沙烏地港口的船隻，首波油輪改道情形也顯示，至少部分營運商已將威脅視為實際作業風險，而非口頭恫嚇。

美國總統川普其後淡化立即展開談判的可能性，表示伊朗在準備進行有意義的接觸前，美國無意會談。這項立場使斡旋工作短期內看不到明確突破，波斯灣盟國對區域安全與經濟活動受損也日益不滿。當日油價與美國公債走勢反映的是敵對行動與航運風險延續，而非談判已確定成功或失敗。

高盛估計，若荷莫茲海峽的運輸干擾持續，布蘭特原油第4季可能突破每桶$120，但這並非其基本情境。高盛的核心預測建立在情勢降溫的假設上，預估第4季油價為$80，明年為$75。兩種路徑差距甚大，說明即使市場僅小幅提高長期供應受阻的機率，也可能在實際通膨數據充分反映影響前推升利率。

聯準會升息定價仍不如7月初積極。期貨顯示下次會議升息機率約25%，月初則約為50%。溫和通膨報告削弱了立即行動的理由，但油價回升使交易員無法排除這項可能性。主席凱文·華許領導下的反應函數尚未明朗，也加深了不確定性：市場已有證據顯示官員關注實際通膨，卻不確定他們面對能源帶動的新一波加速時會多快回應。

貨幣市場基金已縮短投資期限。Crane Data資料顯示，基金持債的加權平均到期日由5月中旬的45天降至40天。即使資產的利率敏感度有限，維持利率不變與重啟升息循環之間的差異仍足以顯著改變再投資利率，因此縮短期限可保留調整彈性。

當日勞動數據向聯準會顯示的是韌性，而非過熱。1.209億名全職受薪工作者的每週薪資中位數達$1,251，較一年前增加4.6%；經季節調整後的薪資中位數由第1季的$1,233升至$1,258。薪資漲幅高於CPI-U的3.9%，使實質薪資維持正成長，既支撐家庭購買力，也使名目勞動成本的持續性仍具政策意義。

各州數據顯示，全國整體穩定之下，變化僅集中於少數地區。全國失業率大致持平於4.2%。德州增加43,400個工作機會，明尼蘇達州增加13,200個，新罕布夏州增加4,500個，西維吉尼亞州則減少9,100個；46州與哥倫比亞特區的非農就業人數基本持平。這種廣度本身不足以支持緊急升息，但也沒有呈現廣泛的勞動市場疲弱，使政策制定者更難忽略油價衝擊。

美國公債走勢的組成與這些相互牽制的事實一致。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1.4個基點，反映通膨補償增加；實質殖利率上升2.2個基點，則顯示所得與就業穩定之際，投資人也要求更高實質報酬。一個月來，10年期殖利率上升17.4個基點，幾乎全數由10年期實質殖利率上升16.9個基點所解釋，同期損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.5個基點。本輪油價衝擊改變了單日通膨訊號，但殖利率較長期的升勢仍主要由實質利率與期限風險壓力推動。

現券市場交易量增加，但未呈現方向性資金流。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額成交額為$8,561億，較7月20日增加3.3%，共325,769筆交易。名目附息債成交額增加7%至$6,665億。原始到期日超過3年、但不逾5年的券種周轉額增加13.3%，2年期以下則增加12.3%，正好對應當日政策定價調整最明顯的曲線區段。實質殖利率與通膨補償同步上升之際，TIPS成交額增加8.6%至$189億。

## 財政疑慮壓抑英國與日本公債

市場首次面對伯納姆政府後，英國公債仍難以回穩。較長天期殖利率一度升至5月中旬以來最高，之後才略為回落；投資人關注新政府將如何為承諾的生活成本援助及可能增加的軍事支出籌資。英鎊下跌0.4%至$1.34以下，是當日主要貨幣中表現最弱者。

希利出任財政大臣帶來部分安定作用，因市場認為相較於立場更明確偏左的其他人選，他在財政上較為穩健，但任命本身未回答資金來源問題。伯納姆先前已表示，將爭取放寬借款與支出規則；希利則支持增加國防支出，並承諾重新調整預算優先順序以降低家庭成本。預期中的家庭能源稅減免，成本約為£8.5億。

市場關注焦點已由初期政治交接轉向政策不確定性。英國的借款成本已是G10最高，公共債務規模約相當於全年經濟產出。完整的借款影響可能要到秋季預算公布後才會明朗，英國公債投資人因此必須衡量每一項新承諾，而長天期市場對缺乏資金來源的財政措施仍相當敏感。

日本內閣提出了完整政策文件，卻未提出完整融資計畫。政府核准一項成長策略，計畫在14年內向特定產業投資¥370兆，目標是協助名目GDP提高至接近¥1,100兆。文件保留政府所稱的「負責任擴張性財政政策」，同時刪除長期沿用的「財政整頓」措辭。

相較6月30日草案，新增的註腳把具體貨幣政策工具交由日本央行決定，並確認央行自主性。文件也表示，適當政策應有助於物價穩定上升，這項措辭容許央行在條件適合時進一步升息。這些增補降低了市場對首相高市早苗意圖阻止進一步政策正常化的疑慮，卻未解決首份草案公布後曾推升殖利率的財政問題。

政府將食品消費稅的決定延後至8月初。高市早苗競選時主張暫停徵收8%的稅率兩年，財務省估計每年將減少約¥5兆收入。官員也曾考慮把稅率降至1%，或永久調降。最終文件未說明這項措施及增加國防支出的資金來源。

政府把衡量財政健全程度的主要指標轉向債務對GDP比率，並表示將在降低該比率的同時決定可行預算規模。這套做法更加重視分母的經濟成長，但投資人仍須評估推動投資與國防計畫所需的公債發行量及利息支出。高市早苗在承認市場疑慮的同時，承諾將以更透明且一致的方式溝通。

需求面證據為長天期債券提供部分支撐。日本壽險與產險公司6月淨買進原始到期日超過10年的債券¥6,305億，創2023年7月以來新高。殖利率已升至足以吸引傳統買家的水準，政府鼓勵本國投資人持有日本資產的提案也可能改善市場情緒。

不過，各期限及投資人類別的需求並不一致。日本央行6月中旬升息25個基點，並承諾在經濟條件適合時持續收緊政策後，海外投資人對原始期限為2年或5年的政府債券賣超規模創2022年12月以來最大。國內保險公司重返超長天期債券，外國投資人則降低接近政策敏感區段的曝險。

日圓走勢顯示匯市中何種壓力占上風。美國殖利率上升、油價走高及日本擴張性財政方向，蓋過確認日本央行獨立性所帶來的安定效果；日圓一度貶值0.5%，至每美元163.24日圓，美元兌日圓自1986年以來首次升破163。日本當局在4月28日至5月27日期間已斥資¥11.73兆干預，但日圓仍處於40年低點。

財務大臣片山皋月近日已強化干預警告，不過日圓貶值步調較為漸進，市場對當局即將採取行動的信心因而下降。日本是能源進口國，日圓走弱與原油上漲的組合格外棘手：政府研議減稅、日本央行評估進一步緊縮之際，進口成本也隨之上升。

歐元區資料顯示，既有緊縮措施已傳導至私人信貸。銀行在第2季收緊企業貸款標準，理由包括經濟前景、風險承擔意願下降，以及對地緣政治與能源情勢的憂慮；房貸、消費信貸及其他家庭貸款的標準也同步收緊。

企業信貸需求略增，主要受到庫存與營運資金、大型企業固定投資，以及再融資與重整需求支撐。相較之下，消費者信心惡化、利率變動及房市預期轉弱，使住房貸款需求明顯下降。這項差異顯示，即使家庭借款對利率日益敏感，企業仍需要資金維持營運及管理資產負債表。

這項調查在歐洲央行為期兩天的會議前公布。繼6月升息25個基點後，預期官員本次將維持利率不變，經濟學家與投資人則預期9月還會再升息。銀行標準收緊與房貸需求轉弱，顯示限制性政策已在發揮作用；但油價高於$90，也使輸入性通膨風險持續存在。市場面對的並非通膨壓力與政策傳導二擇一，而是兩者同時存在。

## 債權人保障左右壓力型信用表現

Aston Martin債券持有人把既有結盟行動升高為直接法律挑戰。部分債權人致函這家汽車製造商，主張一項以移出其求償範圍的資產作擔保之擬議融資，可能違反適用紐約州法律的債券文件。與HPS Investment Partners研議中的交易將採用資產下移結構，可能把智慧財產權等擔保品移出既有債權人的擔保組合。

這封由Quinn Emanuel擬定的信函要求Aston Martin在48小時內確認不會進行此類交易。信中也主張，如果董事會未考慮現有債權人提出的替代融資方案便選擇HPS提案，可能承擔英國法律風險；HPS持有Aston Martin一級方程式車隊權益所形成的關係人問題，也受到點名。

這次行動之所以重要，是因為該債券持有人團體持有Aston Martin於2029年到期、等值$18.5億債券的多數部位，且已簽署合作協議，成員包括Arini Capital Management、BlackRock及Sculptor Capital Management。他們先前曾提出注入新資金並討論更廣泛的資產負債表方案，但表示公司沒有接洽。最新行動使爭議由防禦性的債權人結盟，轉為在擔保品移轉前明確試圖阻止交易。

Aston Martin的流動性壓力源自產品延誤、品質問題、中國需求疲弱及美國關稅。股東先前提供股權支持後，4月又投入£5,000萬債務資金。債權人擔心的不只是公司需要融資，而是寬鬆的文件條款可能讓新資金取得優先求償權，削弱現有擔保品的價值。

Victoria面對的是另一種門檻問題。這家英國地毯製造商表示，持有其2028年到期債券逾75%的投資人支持一項預計減債約£3億的重整方案，但仍低於完成協議重整所需的90%，因此可能轉而採取法院核准程序。

HSBC尚未加入協議。依據條款，現有債券持有人將取得2031年到期的新發第二順位留置權債券，面額相當於現有債券的75%，另可獲得Victoria約19%的股權。取得提前同意費的截止日為週三。既有支持率使公司握有一定談判籌碼，但能否補足至90%的差距，將決定較多價值可否透過協議途徑留給債權人，或會被法院程序消耗。

America’s Car-Mart則顯示營運惡化與融資結構如何相互強化。這家次級汽車經銷商難以籌措新客戶貸款及補充車輛庫存，庫存因而下降52%，汽車銷量減少27%。管理層正尋求新融資，並考慮出售經銷據點或其他資產，最終可能在破產程序內外逐步結束營運。

Car-Mart仰賴資產擔保證券化，貸款承作減少因而演變成流動性限制。2022年至2024年間，公司透過ABS交易借入約$25億；其融資應收款則由2021年的約$8.1億，在四年後增至逾$15億。通膨與高利率削弱客戶財務能力後，信用損失上升，承銷標準收緊也壓低銷售。ABS結構要求收款留在為債券持有人設立的信託內，限制了公司承作替代貸款所能運用的現金。

公司隨後轉向私人信貸。公司10月與Silver Point Capital達成的五年期$3億貸款，利率為SOFR加7.50%，並附帶最高可取得Car-Mart 10%股權的認股權證。該貸款償還了一筆限制嚴格的資產擔保額度，卻未解決公司在貸款承作與證券化之間仍需要倉儲融資額度的問題。

融資努力久未有進展，Car-Mart其後關閉136家經銷據點中的42家並裁減人力。公司6月揭露已對Silver Point貸款違約，使貸款人得以更換董事會，並影響公司是否申請破產保護。公司仍在考慮於美國破產法第11章程序外出售並逐步關閉資產，但尚未選定最終方案。

這個案例具體呈現Oaktree Capital Management對即將到期債務的警告。該公司盤點出約250家借款人的約$2,000億債務，這些債務的交易殖利率高於15%，或價格低於面額的90%。Oaktree董事總經理暨共同投資組合經理Danielle Poli表示，2020年代稍早進行的負債管理交易只是延後、而非消除再融資問題，使硬性到期壓力集中於2027年與2028年。

這項估計並非預測$2,000億債務將全數違約，而是界定一群已反映重大壓力、且在高利率持續時容錯空間更小的借款人。Car-Mart顯示，這種組合可能在到期日來臨前便形成自我強化循環：昂貴的救援融資帶來更嚴格控制，營運疲弱進一步限制一般融資管道，借款人違反條款後，貸款人的影響力隨之增加。

其他交易則顯示，即使違約後，債權保障仍可能改善。約$7.43億武漢當代相關美元債券的持有人，已取得香港法院批准追索額外資產。相關資產包括一家境外單位持有的$1.95億優先票據，以及帳面價值接近$2,860萬的其他資產；作為交換，債權人將放棄其他債務形式下的部分請求權。

任何款項都將補充保證人在中國大陸重整計畫下的回收。該計畫向無擔保債權人支付最高人民幣300萬元現金，超過該金額的債權則置入一個持有武漢當代100%權益的五年期信託。境外安排仍取決於資產能否變現，但法院命令使債券持有人在公司2022年違約後，獲得罕見的額外回收途徑。

在壓力較輕的投機級信用市場，Millikin University為一筆延後發行的$4,900萬市政債增添一座600床學生公寓的相關權利，以強化交易條件。這所伊利諾州大學預計於2027會計年度收購Woods at Millikin，並在2027年3月前為債券持有人設定抵押權。標普給予該債券BB+評等。

這項擔保品並非沒有營運風險。截至2026年6月的七年間，該公寓累計虧損約$1,000萬，部分原因是Millikin曾承諾在入住率達92.5%以前支付空床費用。大學預測，若2026年秋季至2032年秋季的入住率提高約27%，截至2033年6月可創造約$2,500萬淨收入。新生繳納訂金人數達457人，比目標高10%，但這筆交易仍要求投資人相信招生及宿舍使用率將大幅復甦。

## 新興市場主權與融資管道走勢分化

阿根廷在不到三個月內第三度獲調升主權評等。穆迪將評等由Caa1升至B3，並給予正向展望，與惠譽及標普一樣，把阿根廷調升至高度困境類別之上。該國仍處於深度投機級，但本次調升承認違約風險已顯著下降，也擴大了潛在機構投資人範圍。

穆迪列舉的理由包括財政趨穩、出口增強、能源與採礦業外國直接投資增加、外部融資管道改善及治理提升。政府維持財政盈餘，並運用本地法美元債、銀行附買回交易及多邊融資履行債務。央行上半年購入超過$100億外匯，達成政府與國際貨幣基金約定的外匯存底累積目標。

阿根廷主權債相對美國公債利差接近400個基點，為八年來最低。官員主張，財政與外部基本面改善足以支持利差接近250至300個基點。穆迪的正向展望保留進一步升評空間，但也指出2027年總統大選構成風險。穆迪認為潛在政策結果的範圍已縮小，支持政策延續的判斷，卻未消除政治考驗。

印尼追求的是融資多元化，而非評等改善。該國開始行銷首批在中國境內發行的熊貓債，提供3年期及5年期券種，初步合計規模最高人民幣70億元。印尼已獲准在未來兩年發行最高人民幣300億元，簿記建檔定於週四進行。

募集資金將匯至境外作一般融資用途，也可能兌換成其他貨幣。印尼今年已在非美元國際市場籌得約$70億，包括歐元、日圓及離岸人民幣債券，創下此類發行紀錄。首次發行熊貓債可接觸中國境內投資人，但同時印尼盾仍接近歷史低點，高能源成本也對經常帳及燃料補貼形成壓力。

這筆交易並未消除更廣泛的主權疑慮。穆迪與惠譽都以普拉伯沃·蘇比安托總統任內的治理問題為由，在維持評等的同時把印尼展望調為負向。印尼央行已升息以支撐匯率，國內股市則是全球表現最差的市場。中國聯合資信給予印尼熊貓債AAA評等，但國際投資人仍在衡量其國家主導政策議程與外部失衡。

Danantara Investment Management同時研議延長美元債到期結構。這家印尼主權財富基金已委任Citigroup、HSBC、JPMorgan、Mitsubishi UFJ及Standard Chartered，評估市場對20年期及30年期優先票據的需求。該基金6月首次進入國際市場，透過5年期及10年期債券籌得$15億，高於原定$10億目標。

惠譽給予擬議債務BBB評等，穆迪則評為Baa2。第二筆交易將測試市場對Danantara的需求能否延伸至首次發行所採較短期限以外。CreditSights先前認為，首筆交易的報酬未充分補償該基金的負面消息及印尼總體經濟不確定性，因此最終定價與各期限的發行配置，將成為衡量市場信心的重要指標。

奈及利亞評估同一波油價衝擊時，選擇維持政策克制。央行將基準利率維持在26.5%，符合全部7名經濟學家的預測。央行總裁Olayemi Cardoso稱中東敵對行動再起是前景的最大風險，並表示審慎立場仍屬適當。

6月通膨率持平於15.9%，未如預期加速。Cardoso表示，奈及利亞奈拉穩定，加上先前緊縮政策的遞延效果，應可支持通膨進一步放緩；若衝突延長並威脅物價或金融穩定，委員會仍準備採取行動。奈及利亞具備國內煉油能力，並且是石油產品淨出口國，因而獲得部分緩衝，但仍不足以說服政策制定者恢復降息。

俄羅斯財政部面對更直接的融資中斷。該部在取消7月8日標售、並於一週後無法以可接受條件出售證券後，暫停國內政府債券標售。7月迄今僅售出100億盧布OFZ，遠低於第3季1.5兆盧布的發行目標。

上半年預算赤字達5.7兆盧布，相當於GDP的2.5%，已超過全年預算所編列的3.8兆盧布赤字。國內借款是政府5.5兆盧布融資計畫的核心，其中近4兆盧布原預期來自OFZ發行、國家福利基金及民營化。

俄羅斯央行7月24日的決策也成為發債問題的一部分。央行6月把政策利率降至14.25%，但表示進一步寬鬆的空間正在縮小。多數分析師預期利率不變，市場則因國內燃料危機，仍反映相當程度的升息機率。政府債券主要指數在暫停標售後上漲，但7月仍累計下跌約1.2%。

私人市場投資人則未等待公開市場退出，已自行創造流動性。Jefferies資料顯示，上半年由管理人主導的次級市場交易總額達$620億，歐洲基金經理人占24%；該公司估計，歐洲全年交易量可能超過$350億。這些交易把資產移入延續型基金，使既有投資人得以出售、新投資人得以進場，基金經理人則能延長持有期間。

全球次級市場交易量上半年創下$1,180億紀錄，全年預計將超過$2,600億。交易加速反映傳統資產出售及公開發行所帶來的分配有限。此類交易雖可提供流動性，卻只是把資產移入新結構並重設經濟條件，未解決以可接受估值完成退出的根本困難。

## 後續市場意義

歐洲央行7月23日會議將檢驗官員如何權衡能源通膨再起與信貸條件收緊。繼6月升息25個基點後，本次預期維持利率不變。更重要的訊號是，住房貸款需求下降及銀行全面收緊授信標準，是否會降低9月再度升息的可能性，抑或油價高於$90仍使升息選項成為政策指引核心。

美國財政部7月23日將標售$210億新發10年期抗通膨債券，為實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升後的直接考驗。該券7月31日交割，2036年7月15日到期。在市場提高能源帶動通膨反彈的權重之際，投標需求將顯示接近2.35%的10年期實質殖利率是否足以吸引投資人承擔存續期風險。

美國6月新屋銷售將於7月24日公布。房市是高企的美國公債殖利率抑制需求最明確的傳導管道之一，因此這項數據將影響市場如何衡量現有貨幣緊縮程度與未來通膨。銷售疲弱將強化市場借款成本正替聯準會承擔更多緊縮工作的證據；需求若具韌性，政策制定者便更缺乏理由淡化新一波油價衝擊。

7月27日將公布耐久財訂單初值，7月28日則有經濟指標初值。這些數據將顯示企業投資及貿易相關活動是否仍足以支撐較高實質殖利率。隨後的7月28日至29日FOMC會議，將判定市場目前對立即升息約25%的機率，究竟高估或低估官員在能源衝擊充分反映於通膨數據前採取行動的意願。

日本預定在8月初前決定食品消費稅方案。任何減稅的幅度、期間及融資方式，都將影響政府債券供給與日圓，若方案仍與增加國防支出並行，影響尤其明顯。在此之前，美國殖利率與進口能源成本同步上升之際，市場將評估日本政府確認央行自主性是否足以支撐日圓。

印尼週四的熊貓債簿記建檔，將確定其首次在中國境內發行主權債所能取得的條件。市場也會把結果與Danantara研議發行20年期及30年期美元債一併解讀。需求強勁將驗證跨貨幣與投資人基礎多元化的成效；若發行讓利偏大或規模縮減，則顯示印尼盾疲弱、能源曝險及治理疑慮仍限制市場融資能力。

俄羅斯央行7月24日的決策，將決定財政部能否以較可接受的條件恢復OFZ標售。若維持利率不變並提出明確指引，可降低政策不確定性，卻無法消除上半年赤字已超過全年預算所造成的融資需求。標售若持續暫停，更多融資可能轉向替代來源或浮動利率債務。

美國信用市場接下來的壓力點來自契約與流動性。Aston Martin如何回應債權人的法律信函，將決定爭議會進入訴訟，還是轉向更廣泛的融資協商。Victoria必須把逾75%的支持率提高至90%的協議門檻，否則就得準備進入法院程序。Car-Mart在Silver Point貸款違約後，仍需要替代資金或資產出售方案。三者是彼此獨立的信用個案，但都將檢驗高利率使再融資依賴演變為擔保品、控制權與回收價值之爭時，貸款人能否保存價值。

overall_summary.headline: 油價重燃近期聯準會升息風險，美國公債下跌、殖利率曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債延續跌勢，殖利率曲線呈空頭趨平。2年期殖利率上升5.5個基點至4.264%，5年期上升4.8個基點至4.37%，10年期上升3.6個基點至4.629%，30年期上升2個基點至5.133%。2年期與10年期利差收窄1.9個基點至36.5個基點，最大幅度的調整仍集中於聯準會政策展望附近。

油價是最明確的催化因素。美國與伊朗交戰進入第10天，胡塞武裝針對停靠沙烏地港口船隻的威脅也開始改變油輪航線，WTI上漲1.92%至$84.83，布蘭特原油上漲2.87%至$91.78。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1.4個基點至2.279%，10年期實質殖利率則上升2.2個基點至2.35%，顯示投資人既要求補償重燃的通膨風險，也要求持有利率部位取得更高實質報酬。期貨顯示7月28日至29日聯準會會議升息的機率約為25%。

勞動數據呈現韌性，但未見全面加速：第2季每週薪資中位數較一年前上升4.6%，6月多數州的失業率與非農就業人數則大致穩定。半導體股領漲帶動股市走高，即使原油、黃金與美元也同步上漲，美國公債仍未獲得明顯避險買盤。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their selloff on July 21 as another rise in crude oil revived near-term inflation risk and pushed the market toward a greater probability of Federal Reserve tightening. The 2-year yield rose 5.5 basis points to 4.264%, the 5-year added 4.8 basis points to 4.37%, the 10-year increased 3.6 basis points to 4.629%, and the 30-year climbed 2 basis points to 5.133%. The larger adjustment at the front and intermediate parts of the curve narrowed 2s10s by 1.9 basis points to 36.5 basis points and 2s30s by 3.5 basis points to 86.9 basis points.

Oil supplied the clearest catalyst. WTI advanced 1.92% to $84.83 and Brent gained 2.87% to $91.78 as the United States and Iran exchanged strikes for a 10th consecutive day and the threat to Saudi Arabian shipping began to alter tanker behavior. Iran-backed Houthi militants warned that vessels calling at Saudi ports could be targeted. Tankers approaching Yemeni waters paused, while ships carrying Saudi crude turned north toward the Suez Canal. The threat reached a route that had become more important after Saudi Arabia redirected output around the disrupted Strait of Hormuz.

The market response moved beyond inflation compensation. The 10-year breakeven rate rose 1.4 basis points to 2.279%, but the 10-year real yield also increased 2.2 basis points to 2.35%. Investors were charging for both a less favorable inflation outlook and a higher inflation-adjusted return on duration. Interest-rate futures assigned about a 25% probability to an increase at the July 28–29 Fed meeting, up modestly in recent days but below the roughly even odds seen earlier in the month. The bond rally that followed last week’s benign inflation releases has now been erased.

Fresh labor evidence did not offer a broad easing signal. Median weekly earnings for full-time U.S. workers increased 4.6% from a year earlier in Q2, faster than the 3.9% rise in consumer prices. State labor markets were mostly stable in June: unemployment rates fell in 8 states, rose in 2 and were unchanged in 40 states and the District of Columbia, while payrolls increased significantly in only 3 states and fell in 1. The combination preserved household-income support without showing either a nationwide employment acceleration or the kind of deterioration that would clearly offset the energy shock.

Risk assets were resilient enough to deny Treasuries a meaningful haven bid. The S&P 500 gained 0.89%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.93%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.21% as investors returned to beaten-down chipmakers. The semiconductor gauge nevertheless remained 13.85% lower over a month, leaving the rebound as a partial recovery rather than a reversal of the recent reassessment of AI valuations. Gold rose 1.87% to $4,085.20, while the dollar index gained 0.19%. The simultaneous advances in stocks, oil, gold and the dollar left the rates market focused on inflation and policy rather than on a uniform retreat from risk.

Outside the United States, sovereign curves carried their own sources of pressure. UK yields remained near 2-month highs as investors waited for new Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey to reconcile cost-of-living and defense promises with limited fiscal space. Japan’s final economic plan affirmed Bank of Japan autonomy but did not resolve the cost or financing of a proposed food-tax cut. Euro-area banks reported tighter lending standards across corporate and household credit. Together, those developments reinforced a global environment in which higher energy costs are arriving while fiscal room is contested and the transmission of earlier monetary tightening remains active.

Credit continued to differentiate among improving sovereigns, borrowers with access to new pools of capital and companies whose documentation or liquidity had become the main source of value. Moody’s upgraded Argentina, Indonesia opened books for its first panda bonds, and Danantara explored another dollar issue. At the stressed end, Aston Martin creditors escalated their opposition to a potential collateral transfer, Victoria remained short of the support needed for a consensual restructuring, and America’s Car-Mart weighed asset sales after defaulting on a private loan. High benchmark yields have not closed financing markets, but they are exposing borrowers that depend on repeated refinancing, permissive covenants or optimistic operating assumptions.

## Oil Restores Immediate Federal Reserve Risk

The Treasury move was a bearish flattening rather than a repeat of the previous session’s modest steepening. The 2-year yield’s 5.5-basis-point increase exceeded the 30-year move by 3.5 basis points, showing that the marginal repricing concentrated on the policy horizon. The 10-year reached 4.64% intraday, its highest level since late May, while the 10- and 30-year sectors both finished around 2-month highs.

The oil advance made the timing of the inflation risk more immediate. Brent closed above $91 after the renewed fighting and threats to Red Sea shipping, extending its gain to 8.32% over a week and 14.94% over a month. WTI was 6.92% higher over a week and 10.74% higher over a month. Those cumulative moves matter for the Fed because the favorable June inflation readings captured an earlier energy backdrop, while the market is now assessing the possible pass-through from a sustained July rebound.

The security problem also widened geographically. Hormuz traffic was already under pressure from attacks and the war with Iran. Saudi Arabia had used cross-desert pipelines and Red Sea terminals to preserve exports, making that route an important buffer for global supply. The Houthi warning threatened ships traveling to and from Saudi ports, and the first changes in tanker routes showed that at least some operators were treating the threat as operational rather than rhetorical.

President Donald Trump later minimized the prospect of immediate talks, saying the United States had no interest in meeting until Iran was prepared for meaningful engagement. That stance left mediation efforts without a clear near-term breakthrough while Gulf allies grew increasingly frustrated with the damage to regional security and economic activity. The completed oil and Treasury moves reflected the continuation of hostilities and shipping risk rather than a confirmed failure or success of negotiations.

Goldman Sachs estimated that Brent could exceed $120 a barrel by Q4 if disruption through Hormuz persists, although that was not its base case. Its central forecast was $80 in Q4 and $75 next year on an assumption of de-escalation. The distance between those paths illustrates why even a modest change in the probability of prolonged disruption can move rates before realized inflation data show the full effect.

The Fed pricing remained less aggressive than it had been earlier in July. Futures implied about a 25% chance of an increase at the coming meeting, compared with roughly 50% earlier in the month. Benign inflation reports reduced the case for acting immediately, but the recovery in oil has prevented traders from dismissing the option. The uncertainty is amplified by an unsettled reaction function under Chair Kevin Warsh: the market has evidence that officials are focused on realized inflation, but less confidence about how quickly they would respond to a renewed energy-driven acceleration.

Money-market funds have reacted by shortening exposure. The weighted-average maturity of fund holdings fell to 40 days from 45 days in mid-May, according to Crane Data. The move preserves flexibility when the difference between a hold and a renewed tightening cycle can materially alter reinvestment rates even for assets with limited duration.

The day’s labor releases offered the Fed evidence of resilience rather than overheating. Median weekly earnings reached $1,251 for 120.9 million full-time wage and salary workers, 4.6% above a year earlier. Seasonally adjusted median earnings rose to $1,258 from $1,233 in Q1. Because earnings outpaced the 3.9% increase in CPI-U, real wage growth remained positive, supporting household purchasing power while keeping nominal labor-cost persistence relevant.

State data showed narrow changes beneath a stable national picture. The national unemployment rate was little changed at 4.2%. Texas added 43,400 jobs, Minnesota 13,200 and New Hampshire 4,500, while West Virginia lost 9,100. Payrolls were essentially unchanged in 46 states and the District of Columbia. That breadth does not support an urgent tightening case on its own, but neither does it provide a broad labor-market weakening signal that would make an oil shock easier for policymakers to disregard.

The composition of the Treasury move was consistent with those competing facts. A 1.4-basis-point rise in the 10-year breakeven reflected more inflation compensation, while the 2.2-basis-point increase in the real yield showed that investors also required a higher real return as income and employment remained stable. Over a month, the 10-year yield has risen 17.4 basis points, almost entirely matched by a 16.9-basis-point increase in the 10-year real yield; the breakeven is only 0.5 basis point higher over that period. The current oil shock altered the daily inflation signal, but the broader rise in yields has been dominated by real-rate and term-risk pressure.

Cash-market activity increased without showing directional flow. FINRA recorded $856.1 billion of Treasury par transactions, 3.3% more than on July 20, across 325,769 trades. Nominal-coupon activity rose 7% to $666.5 billion. Turnover increased 13.3% in maturities longer than 3 years and no more than 5 years and 12.3% in maturities of 2 years or less, matching the parts of the curve where the day’s policy adjustment was most visible. TIPS activity rose 8.6% to $18.9 billion as real yields and inflation compensation both moved higher.

## Fiscal Questions Hold Up UK and Japanese Duration

UK gilts struggled to recover after the market’s first encounter with Burnham’s government. Longer yields had reached their highest levels since mid-May before easing, with investors focused on how the new administration would finance promised cost-of-living relief and possible increases in military spending. Sterling fell 0.4% to below $1.34, the weakest performance among major peers on the day.

Healey’s appointment as chancellor offered some reassurance because he was viewed as a safer fiscal choice than more explicitly left-wing alternatives. It did not answer the funding question. Burnham had already said he would seek flexibility in the rules governing borrowing and spending, while Healey has supported higher defense expenditure and pledged reprioritization to lower household costs. An expected cut in household energy taxes would cost about £850 million.

The policy uncertainty has replaced the initial political transition as the market’s concern. Britain already has the highest borrowing costs in the Group of 10 and public debt around the size of annual output. The full borrowing implications are unlikely to be known before the autumn budget, leaving gilt investors to assess each new pledge against a long-end market still sensitive to unfunded fiscal measures.

Japan’s cabinet delivered a completed policy document, but not a complete financing plan. The government approved a growth strategy calling for ¥370 trillion of investment across selected industries over 14 years, intended to help lift nominal gross domestic product to almost ¥1,100 trillion. It also retained the administration’s description of a responsible expansionary fiscal policy while dropping the long-standing phrase “fiscal consolidation.”

A footnote added since the June 30 draft left specific monetary tools to the BOJ and affirmed the central bank’s autonomy. The document also said appropriate policy should contribute to stable price increases, wording that allows further rate increases if conditions warrant. Those additions reduced concern that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi intended to prevent additional normalization, but they did not resolve the fiscal questions that had pushed yields higher after the first draft.

The government postponed its decision on the food sales tax until early August. Takaichi had campaigned on suspending the 8% tax for 2 years, a measure the Finance Ministry estimated would reduce revenue by about ¥5 trillion annually. Officials have also considered cutting the rate to 1% or making the reduction permanent. The final document did not explain how the measure or higher defense spending would be financed.

The government shifted the primary measure of fiscal health toward the debt-to-GDP ratio and said it would determine feasible budget size while reducing that ratio. That approach gives greater weight to growth in the denominator, but investors still have to assess the amount of bond issuance and interest expense required to deliver the investment and defense programs. Takaichi promised more transparent and consistent communication, while acknowledging market concern.

Demand evidence offered some support for the long end. Japanese life and casualty insurers bought a net ¥630.5 billion of bonds with original maturities longer than 10 years in June, the most since July 2023. Yields had risen to levels that attracted a traditional buyer, and government proposals to encourage domestic ownership of Japanese assets may also have helped sentiment.

The demand was not uniform across maturities or investor groups. Overseas investors sold the most government notes with original 2- or 5-year maturities since December 2022 after the BOJ raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in mid-June and pledged to keep tightening when economic conditions warranted. Domestic insurers were returning to super-long bonds while foreign investors reduced exposure near the policy-sensitive part of the curve.

The yen showed which pressure was dominant in the currency market. It weakened as much as 0.5% to 163.24 per dollar, crossing 163 for the first time since 1986 as rising U.S. yields, higher oil and Japan’s expansionary fiscal direction overwhelmed the reassurance on BOJ independence. Japanese authorities had spent ¥11.73 trillion intervening between April 28 and May 27, but the currency remained at a 4-decade low.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama had recently strengthened her intervention warning, although the gradual pace of depreciation reduced confidence that action was imminent. Japan’s status as an energy importer makes the combination of a weaker yen and higher crude especially difficult: it raises imported costs even as the government is considering tax relief and the central bank is assessing further tightening.

Euro-area evidence showed that existing restraint is already reaching private credit. Banks tightened standards for corporate loans in Q2, citing the economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance and concern over geopolitical and energy developments. They also tightened standards for mortgages, consumer credit and other household lending.

Corporate demand for credit increased slightly, supported by inventories and working capital, fixed investment by large companies, and refinancing and restructuring needs. Housing-loan demand, by contrast, declined markedly as consumer confidence deteriorated, interest rates changed and housing-market expectations weakened. The difference suggests that companies still need funding for operations and balance-sheet management even as household borrowing becomes more rate-sensitive.

The survey arrived ahead of the ECB’s 2-day meeting. Officials are expected to hold rates after a 25-basis-point increase in June, while economists and investors anticipate another move in September. Tighter bank standards and weaker mortgage demand show restraint already operating, but oil above $90 keeps imported inflation risk alive. The choice is therefore not between active inflation pressure and no policy transmission; both are present.

## Creditor Protections Define the Stressed End of Credit

Aston Martin’s bondholders escalated an existing organization effort into a direct legal challenge. Some creditors sent the automaker a letter asserting that a proposed financing backed by assets moved beyond their reach could violate its New York-law bond documents. The contemplated transaction with HPS Investment Partners would use a drop-down structure that could remove collateral, including intellectual property, from the existing creditors’ security package.

The letter, prepared by Quinn Emanuel, gave Aston Martin 48 hours to confirm that it would not proceed with such a transaction. It also argued that the board could face risks under English law if it selected the HPS proposal without considering an alternative financing offered by current creditors, and highlighted the related-party issue created by HPS’s ownership interest in Aston Martin’s Formula One team.

The escalation matters because the bondholder group holds a majority of Aston Martin’s $1.85 billion-equivalent of notes due in 2029 and has signed a cooperation agreement. Members include Arini Capital Management, BlackRock and Sculptor Capital Management. They previously offered fresh capital and broader balance-sheet discussions, but said the company did not engage. Their latest action moves the dispute from defensive organization to an explicit attempt to stop a transaction before collateral is transferred.

Aston Martin’s liquidity pressure reflects product delays, quality problems, weak demand in China and U.S. tariffs. Shareholders supplied £50 million of debt in April after earlier equity support. The concern for bondholders is not merely that the company needs financing, but that permissive documentation could allow new money to gain superior claims and impair the value of their existing collateral.

Victoria faced a different threshold problem. The UK carpet maker said holders of more than 75% of its 2028 notes supported a restructuring designed to reduce debt by about £300 million. That remained below the 90% needed to complete the deal consensually, leaving a court-sanctioned process as a possible alternative.

HSBC had not joined the agreement. Under its terms, existing noteholders would receive new second-lien bonds due in 2031 with face value equal to 75% of their current notes, plus about 19% of Victoria’s equity. The deadline to qualify for an early-bird fee was Wednesday. The support already obtained gives the company leverage, but the gap to 90% determines whether more value can remain with bondholders through a consensual route or be consumed by a court process.

America’s Car-Mart illustrated how operating deterioration and financing structure can reinforce each other. Inventory fell 52% and vehicle sales declined 27% as the subprime auto dealer struggled to fund new customer loans and replenish its lots. Management was seeking fresh financing and considering dealership or other asset sales that could ultimately produce a wind-down, either inside or outside bankruptcy.

Car-Mart’s dependence on asset-backed securitization turned weaker originations into a liquidity constraint. It borrowed roughly $2.5 billion through ABS transactions from 2022 through 2024 as finance receivables grew from about $810 million in 2021 to more than $1.5 billion 4 years later. When inflation and higher rates weakened its customers, credit losses rose and tighter underwriting reduced sales. The ABS structures required collections to remain in trusts for bondholders, limiting the cash available to originate replacement loans.

The company then turned to private credit. A 5-year, $300 million Silver Point Capital loan agreed in October carried interest of SOFR plus 7.50% and warrants for as much as 10% of Car-Mart’s equity. The loan repaid a restrictive asset-backed line, but did not solve the need for a warehouse facility bridging loan origination and securitization.

Car-Mart subsequently closed 42 of its 136 dealerships and reduced staff as the financing effort dragged on. It disclosed in June that it had defaulted on the Silver Point loan, allowing the lender to change the board and influence whether the company seeks bankruptcy protection. A sale and gradual closure of assets outside Chapter 11 remained under consideration, although no final plan had been selected.

The case gives concrete form to Oaktree Capital Management’s warning about approaching maturities. The firm identified about $200 billion of debt from 250 borrowers trading at yields above 15% or prices below 90 cents on the dollar. Danielle Poli, an Oaktree managing director and co-portfolio manager, said liability-management transactions earlier in the decade postponed rather than eliminated refinancing problems, leaving hard maturities concentrated in 2027 and 2028.

That estimate is not a forecast that all $200 billion will default. It defines a group already priced for material stress and facing a smaller margin for error if rates stay high. Car-Mart shows how the combination can become self-reinforcing before a maturity date arrives: expensive rescue financing imposes tighter controls, weaker operations reduce access to ordinary funding, and the lender gains influence when the borrower breaches its terms.

Other transactions demonstrated that protection can improve even after a default. Holders of about $743 million of Wuhan Dangdai-related dollar notes received Hong Kong court approval to pursue additional assets. The assets include $195 million of senior notes held by an offshore unit and other holdings with a book value near $28.6 million. In exchange, creditors would waive some claims in other forms of debt.

Any payout would supplement recoveries under the guarantor’s mainland restructuring plan. That plan pays unsecured creditors cash up to 3 million yuan and places claims above that amount into a 5-year trust holding a 100% interest in Wuhan Dangdai. The offshore arrangement remains conditional on realization of the assets, but the court order gives bondholders a rare route to additional recovery after the company’s 2022 defaults.

At the less distressed edge of speculative credit, Millikin University strengthened a delayed $49 million municipal bond offering by adding rights over a 600-bed student apartment complex. The Illinois university expects to acquire the Woods at Millikin in fiscal 2027 and provide bondholders with a mortgage by March 2027. S&P rated the bonds BB+.

The collateral is not free of operating risk. The apartment complex lost about $10 million over the 7 years through June 2026, partly because Millikin had guaranteed payments for vacant beds up to a 92.5% occupancy rate. The university projects roughly $25 million of net revenue through June 2033 if occupancy rises about 27% between fall 2026 and fall 2032. Freshman deposits of 457 exceeded its goal by 10%, but the deal still asks investors to rely on a substantial recovery in enrollment and housing use.

## Sovereign and Funding Access Diverges Across Emerging Markets

Argentina received its third sovereign upgrade in less than 3 months. Moody’s raised the rating to B3 from Caa1 and assigned a positive outlook, joining Fitch and S&P in moving the country above the highly distressed category. Argentina remains deeply speculative grade, but the change broadens the potential institutional investor base and recognizes a material reduction in default risk.

Moody’s cited fiscal stabilization, stronger exports, rising foreign direct investment in energy and mining, improved external financing access and better governance. The government has maintained fiscal surpluses while using local-law dollar debt, bank repos and multilateral financing to meet obligations. The central bank purchased more than $10 billion of foreign currency in the first half, satisfying the government’s reserve-accumulation target with the International Monetary Fund.

Argentine sovereign spreads were near 400 basis points over Treasuries, their lowest in 8 years. Officials argued that improving fiscal and external fundamentals justified a range closer to 250–300 basis points. Moody’s positive outlook leaves room for further upgrades, but it also identified risk around the 2027 presidential election. Its assessment that the range of potential policy outcomes has narrowed supports continuity without eliminating the political test.

Indonesia pursued diversification rather than a ratings improvement. The sovereign began marketing its first onshore Chinese panda bonds, offering 3- and 5-year maturities with a combined initial size of as much as 7 billion yuan. It has approval to issue as much as 30 billion yuan over the next 2 years, and bookbuilding is scheduled for Thursday.

Proceeds will be remitted offshore for general funding and may be converted into other currencies. Indonesia has already raised about $7 billion this year in non-dollar international markets, including euros, yen and offshore yuan, a record for such issuance. The panda debut adds access to China’s domestic investor base while the rupiah remains near record lows and high energy costs pressure the current account and fuel subsidies.

The transaction does not remove broader sovereign concerns. Moody’s and Fitch have cut Indonesia’s outlook to negative while affirming its rating, citing governance under President Prabowo Subianto. Bank Indonesia has raised rates to support the currency, and the domestic stock market has been the world’s weakest performer. China Lianhe assigned Indonesia a AAA rating for the panda transaction, but international investors continue to weigh the state-centered policy agenda and external imbalance.

Danantara Investment Management simultaneously explored extending its dollar maturity profile. Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund hired Citigroup, HSBC, JPMorgan, Mitsubishi UFJ and Standard Chartered to assess demand for 20- and 30-year senior notes. The mandate followed its $1.5 billion international debut in June, which exceeded an original $1 billion target through 5- and 10-year bonds.

Fitch assigned the proposed debt BBB and Moody’s Baa2. The second transaction would test whether demand for Danantara extends beyond the shorter maturities used in its debut. CreditSights had argued that the first deal did not fully compensate investors for the fund’s negative headlines and Indonesia’s macroeconomic uncertainty, making final pricing and tenor distribution important measures of market confidence.

Nigeria chose policy restraint as it assessed the same oil shock. Its central bank held the benchmark rate at 26.5%, matching all 7 economist forecasts. Governor Olayemi Cardoso called renewed Middle East hostilities the largest risk to the outlook and said a cautious stance remained appropriate.

Inflation was unchanged at 15.9% in June rather than accelerating as expected. Cardoso said a stable naira and the lagged effect of previous tightening should support further moderation, while the committee remained prepared to act if a prolonged conflict threatened prices or financial stability. Nigeria’s domestic refining capacity and position as a net exporter of petroleum products provide some insulation, but did not persuade policymakers to resume easing.

Russia’s Finance Ministry confronted a more direct funding disruption. It suspended domestic government-bond auctions after canceling the July 8 sale and failing to place securities a week later at acceptable terms. Only 10 billion rubles of OFZs had been sold during July, against a Q3 issuance target of 1.5 trillion rubles.

The budget deficit reached 5.7 trillion rubles, or 2.5% of GDP, in the first half, already exceeding the full-year budgeted shortfall of 3.8 trillion rubles. Domestic borrowing is central to the government’s 5.5 trillion-ruble financing program, almost 4 trillion rubles of which was expected to come from OFZ issuance, the National Wellbeing Fund and privatization.

The Bank of Russia’s July 24 decision has become part of the issuance problem. The central bank cut its policy rate to 14.25% in June but said the room for further easing was narrowing. Most analysts expected no change, while markets retained a meaningful probability of an increase because of the domestic fuel crisis. The main government-bond index rose after the auction suspension but remained about 1.2% lower for July.

In private markets, investors were creating liquidity without waiting for public exits. European fund managers accounted for 24% of the $62 billion of manager-led secondary transactions in the first half, according to Jefferies, and the firm estimated that European volume could exceed $35 billion for the full year. The transactions move assets into continuation vehicles, allowing existing investors to sell, new investors to enter and managers to retain holdings for longer.

Global secondary-market volume reached a record $118 billion in the first half and was projected to exceed $260 billion for the year. The acceleration reflects limited distributions from conventional asset sales and public offerings. It provides liquidity, but also transfers assets into new structures and resets their economic terms rather than resolving the underlying difficulty of achieving exits at acceptable valuations.

## Forward Market Significance

The ECB meeting on July 23 will test how officials balance renewed energy inflation against tightening credit conditions. A hold is expected after June’s 25-basis-point increase. The more consequential signal will be whether the decline in housing-loan demand and the broad tightening of bank standards reduce the likelihood of another increase in September, or whether oil above $90 keeps that option central to the guidance.

The U.S. Treasury’s $21 billion auction of new 10-year inflation-protected securities on July 23 will provide a direct test after both real yields and breakevens increased. The issue settles July 31 and matures July 15, 2036. Demand will show whether a 10-year real yield near 2.35% is sufficient to absorb duration while the market assigns more weight to an energy-driven inflation rebound.

June U.S. new-home sales arrive July 24. Housing is one of the clearest channels through which elevated Treasury yields can restrain demand, making the release important to the balance between current monetary tightness and prospective inflation. Weak sales would strengthen the evidence that market borrowing costs are doing more of the Fed’s work; resilient demand would leave policymakers with less reason to discount the renewed oil shock.

Advance durable-goods orders follow on July 27 and advance economic indicators on July 28. Those releases will show whether business investment and trade-related activity remain firm enough to sustain higher real yields. The July 28–29 FOMC meeting will then determine whether the roughly 25% probability assigned to an immediate increase overstated or understated officials’ readiness to respond before the energy shock appears fully in inflation data.

Japan’s decision on the food sales tax is due by early August. The size, duration and financing of any reduction will matter for government-bond supply and for the yen, especially if the plan remains paired with higher defense spending. Before then, the market will assess whether the government’s recognition of BOJ autonomy is sufficient to support the currency when U.S. yields and imported energy costs are rising.

Indonesia’s panda-bond bookbuilding on Thursday will establish the terms available for its first domestic Chinese sovereign issue. The result will be read alongside Danantara’s exploration of 20- and 30-year dollar bonds. Strong demand would validate diversification across currencies and investor bases; a large concession or reduced size would show that rupiah weakness, energy exposure and governance concerns still constrain market access.

Russia’s July 24 central-bank decision will determine whether the Finance Ministry can resume OFZ auctions on more acceptable terms. A hold accompanied by clear guidance could reduce policy uncertainty, but it would not eliminate the funding requirement created by a first-half deficit already larger than the full-year budget. Continued auction suspensions would push more financing toward alternative sources or floating-rate debt.

For U.S. credit, the next pressure points are contractual and liquidity-driven. Aston Martin’s response to its creditors’ legal letter will determine whether the dispute moves into litigation or broader financing negotiations. Victoria must either close the gap between support above 75% and the 90% consensual threshold or prepare for a court process. Car-Mart still needs replacement capital or an asset-sale plan after its Silver Point default. These are separate credits, but each will test whether lenders can preserve value when high rates turn refinancing dependence into a contest over collateral, control and recovery.

Nigeria held rates at 26.5%, while Russia suspended bond auctions after weak demand collided with a widening fiscal deficit.

The next tests span policy transmission, inflation protection and Fed reaction. The ECB must weigh tighter bank credit against oil above $90, the July 23 TIPS auction will test demand near a 2.35% real yield, and U.S. housing and durable-goods data will frame the July 28–29 FOMC decision. Fiscal and funding outcomes in Japan, Indonesia and Russia remain separate tests of sovereign-market access.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off and flatten as oil revives near-term Fed tightening risk
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their selloff in a bearish flattening. The 2-year yield rose 5.5 basis points to 4.264%, the 5-year added 4.8 basis points to 4.37%, the 10-year increased 3.6 basis points to 4.629% and the 30-year climbed 2 basis points to 5.133%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 1.9 basis points to 36.5 basis points as the largest adjustment remained concentrated near the Fed policy horizon.

Oil was the clearest catalyst. WTI advanced 1.92% to $84.83 and Brent gained 2.87% to $91.78 as U.S.-Iran fighting continued for a 10th day and Houthi threats against vessels calling at Saudi ports began to alter tanker routes. The 10-year breakeven rose 1.4 basis points to 2.279%, while the 10-year real yield increased 2.2 basis points to 2.35%, showing that investors required compensation for both renewed inflation risk and a higher real return on duration. Futures assigned about a 25% probability to an increase at the July 28–29 Fed meeting.

Labor data showed resilience without broad acceleration: median weekly earnings rose 4.6% from a year earlier in Q2, and most state unemployment rates and payrolls were stable in June. Equities rallied, led by semiconductors, denying Treasuries a meaningful haven bid even as oil, gold and the dollar also advanced.

Fiscal uncertainty kept pressure on UK and Japanese duration, while tighter euro-area lending standards showed that earlier monetary restraint was still reaching private credit. In stressed credit, Aston Martin, Victoria and America’s Car-Mart faced distinct contests over collateral, restructuring consent and liquidity, even as Argentina’s upgrade and Indonesia’s planned panda bonds showed that sovereign funding access remained open for improving or diversifying borrowers.
